approved: Northern Australia Infrastructure Facility Amendment (Extension and Other Measures) Bill 2021
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill would give the Northern Australia Infrastructure Facility more time and flexibility to fund projects in northern Australia.
It would extend the Facility's investment period until 30 June 2026, improve its governance, and make it faster and more adaptable in providing financial help.
The bill follows a statutory review that found the Facility could do more to support economic and population growth in the region.
Extends the Facility's investment period by five years to 30 June 2026.
Increases the scope, speed and flexibility of the Facility's financial assistance for economic infrastructure.
The Northern Australia Infrastructure Facility and projects contributing to northern Australia's economic and population growth.

The Northern Australia Infrastructure Facility (NAIF) has spent only $218.4 million of its $5 billion budget, representing just 5% of promised funds, with fewer than ten projects completed. The speaker supported the bill to extend NAIF to 2026, expand eligible activities, and allow direct lending, while moving a second reading amendment to note the government's failure and call for faster funding release.

The Northern Australia Infrastructure Facility has released only $218.4 million of its $5 billion allocation, and the bill is a necessary response to the government’s failure to get funds out the door. The speaker supported the five-year extension and smaller-project changes, while criticising the government’s record and noting apparent inconsistencies in the minister’s job and funding figures.

The Northern Australia Infrastructure Facility (NAIF) has been a failure, spending only $218 million of its $5 billion budget in five years; the speaker welcomed the bill's changes to broaden funding purposes and allow direct funding to proponents, but stressed the need for Northern Territory and First Nations representation on the NAIF board.

The speaker supported the Northern Australia Infrastructure Facility Amendment (Extension and Other Measures) Bill 2021, arguing it would expand NAIF to make equity investments (capped at $500 million) and fund non-physical infrastructure, citing $2.8 billion in commitments and specific Townsville projects including $35 million for the Cowboys' training centre, $96 million and $46 million for James Cook University, $20 million for Mater Hospital car park, and $50 million for airport redevelopment, while criticising the Queensland Labor state government for delaying approvals.

The speaker supported the Northern Australia Infrastructure Facility Amendment Bill but argued for two changes: a mandated First Nations representative on the NAIF board, and the inclusion of Christmas Island and the Cocos (Keeling) Islands (Indian Ocean Territories) as part of northern Australia for NAIF access, citing their proximity to Darwin and critical infrastructure needs.

The speaker opposed the Northern Australia Infrastructure Facility Amendment Bill, arguing it weakens the NAIF's independence, removes state vetoes, and risks funding fossil fuel projects like the Beetaloo Basin, which could become stranded assets. They noted the bill expands NAIF functions to equity investments and derivatives, with $2.3 billion in remaining funds potentially misused on projects the market won't support.

The speaker argued that the Northern Australia Infrastructure Facility Amendment Bill 2021 is a slush fund for the gas industry, diverting public money from schools and hospitals to fossil fuel projects during a climate crisis. They opposed expanding the NAIF’s scope, including bypassing state vetoes, equity investments, and derivatives, and pledged Greens amendments to require climate and environmental assessments.

The Northern Australia Infrastructure Facility Amendment (Extension and Other Measures) Bill 2021 extends the NAIF’s active investment period and introduces reforms to accelerate lending, enable direct lending to proponents, invest in on-lending partnerships, and expand investment flexibility, including equity investments. The NAIF has made $2.8 billion in investment decisions, and a correction to the explanatory memorandum was tabled.

The speaker moved amendments to the Northern Australia Infrastructure Facility Amendment Bill to remove the Department Secretary from the NAIF board and prohibit financial assistance for fossil fuel-based infrastructure, arguing this would prevent government control and taxpayer losses on risky fossil fuel ventures.

The speaker opposed amendments that would exempt equity investments from the requirement to have written terms and conditions, noting this could allow government stakes in fossil fuel projects without a formal agreement.
